overview: This file concerns Turkish action against Japanese news-agency and newspaper correspondents during World War II. Four telegrams report the expulsions of Eti Moto, the Istanbul correspondent of the Nichi Nichi Shimbun, in November 1942, and Oda, the Istanbul correspondent of the Domei agency, in January 1944. The stated grounds include suspected espionage, photographing military zones, sensational reporting of an impending Turkish coup, abuse of journalistic ethics, and misuse of government facilities. A Department of State transmission memorandum and its enclosed paraphrase show that the information about Eti Moto was circulated to U.S. military, naval, and federal intelligence agencies.

people.name: Robert F. Kelley
people.role: U.S. diplomatic official in Ankara and signatory of the telegrams on Eti Moto's expulsion

people.name: Eti Moto
people.role: Japanese Istanbul correspondent of the Nichi Nichi Shimbun

people.name: Honaker
people.role: U.S. consular official in Istanbul and signatory of the November 19 telegram

people.name: Şükrü Kaya

people.name: Oda
people.role: Japanese Istanbul correspondent of the Domei news agency

subfiles.title: Telegram from Kelley on expulsion of the Nichi Nichi correspondent
subfiles.from: Robert F. Kelley, U.S. Embassy, Ankara
subfiles.about: Reports that Turkey expelled the Istanbul correspondent of the Nichi Nichi Shimbun to Bulgaria on ten hours' notice.
subfiles.summary: Turkish press official told the embassy he expelled the Nichi Nichi correspondent to Bulgaria, facetiously citing attempts to outdo sensational American correspondents.

subfiles.title: Telegram from Honaker on Eti Moto's expulsion
subfiles.about: Reports that Eti Moto was expelled from Turkey after suspected espionage and alleged photography in military zones.
subfiles.summary: A source told Honaker that correspondent Eti Moto was expelled from Turkey, recently suspected of espionage, with photographing military zones the immediate offense.

subfiles.title: Department of State intelligence transmission concerning Eti Moto
subfiles.to: Military Intelligence Division; Office of Naval Intelligence; Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.about: Transmits the confidential report about Eti Moto to three U.S. intelligence and investigative agencies.
subfiles.summary: State forwarded Istanbul information on Eti Moto to Military Intelligence, Naval Intelligence, and the FBI, paraphrasing a confidential November 1942 telegram.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Istanbul telegram no. 313
subfiles.about: Paraphrases the confidential telegram reporting Eti Moto's expulsion for alleged military-zone photography.
subfiles.summary: Paraphrase states Eti Moto, Nichi Nichi correspondent, was expelled from Turkey for photographing military zones, after earlier espionage suspicion, from a confidential source.

subfiles.title: Supplementary telegram explaining Eti Moto's expulsion
subfiles.from: Robert F. Kelley, U.S. Embassy, Ankara
subfiles.about: Clarifies that sensational political reporting, rather than espionage suspicions alone, was the immediate cause of the correspondent's expulsion.
subfiles.summary: Turkish official confirmed Nichi Nichi correspondent's espionage suspicion but cited a sensational dispatch predicting a coup installing Şükrü Kaya as the real expulsion reason.

subfiles.title: Telegram on expulsion of Domei correspondent Oda
subfiles.about: Reports the Turkish Press Bureau's decision to expel Japanese Domei correspondent Oda from Istanbul.
subfiles.summary: Turkish Press Bureau expelled Domei correspondent Oda, accusing him of abusing journalistic ethics and misusing Turkish government facilities, without alleging espionage.

interest: Shows Turkey's wartime expulsion of Japanese correspondents on shifting espionage, photography, and sensational-reporting pretexts.
